_meta.why_v2: Ground-up rebuild, installed from an owner-supplied rewrite per audit/REWRITE-INSTALL-KIT.md. Replaces the nine-mode subscription suite (Sweep/Radar/Optimize/Negotiate/Splits/Trials/Budgets/Tracker/Timeline — keep/cancel verdicts, cost-per-use math from rough frequency labels, invented cancellation steps/scripts/retention tactics naming real company processes and phone numbers, 'wasted money' framing, guilt/permission copy) with one job: turn a recurring-charge list into a short review that groups subscriptions into three review-priority buckets (start_here / take_another_look / probably_leave_alone) and asks one decision-changing question for anything non-obvious. The v1 cases below (main-audit, analyze-six-subs-de, optimize-four-subs-en, negotiate-vodafone-de) tested actions and fields (wasted_monthly, cancellation_script, retention_tactics, optimize/negotiate actions) that no longer exist and were replaced wholesale.
_meta.why_v2_1: 2026-09-12, live-testing correction after v2 shipped: the question field was reconfirming information the visitor already supplied (asking a 'forgot about it' subscription whether it 'became a background charge', when forgot about it already says that) and, separately, assuming an unstated capability — 'would pausing and restarting then cost less?' on a seasonal-use subscription the visitor never said could be paused. The v2 capture below (design-software item 3) is the exact case that surfaced the pause/restart assumption; this recapture confirms the fix. BEFORE YOU DECIDE replaced QUESTION with an explicit 'ask only what's missing, never reconfirm' rule plus a dedicated seasonal-use wrong/right example, verified clean across 6 repeated live runs before recapture.
_meta.how_to_regression_diff: Re-run cases (npm run check:golden subscription-tamer). Diff for QUALITY not exact match: HTTP 200, no truncation. GUARDS: validateResult() in backend/routes/subscription-tamer.js pins every item's bucket to the fixed three-value enum (falls back to a usage-derived bucket, never crashes), force-nulls question for probably_leave_alone, and totals are always recomputed in code from the actual submitted subscriptions, never trusted from the model. The epistemic discipline itself — no 'wasted' language, no keep/cut verdicts, no invented cancellation difficulty/steps/retention offers/current plans, no cost-per-use from a rough usage label, no population claims about subscription creep, no assumed pause/downgrade/restart capability, no reconfirming a fact the visitor already supplied — is prompt-enforced (CONTRACT), not code-checkable. When eyeballing new captures, check that no item names a specific cancellation process, discount offer, or company policy the visitor never supplied, and that no question assumes the service can be paused/restarted or simply re-asks what the usage label already said. DO NOT reverse: the bucket enum whitelist, the recomputed totals, or the CONTRACT disciplines above.
